blocks.heading: Inclusive participation in production
blocks.text: Women and people living with impairments contribute skills, knowledge, enterprise and labour to production. Capabilities vary among individuals, so allocate work using relevant abilities and role needs rather than assumptions based on gender or impairment. Inaccessible workplaces, unsuitable equipment, exclusion from learning or stereotypes can waste available talent. Accessible layouts, suitable tools, fair development opportunities and appropriate task organisation can enable contribution. Inclusion is not a claim that every person performs every task identically; it means assessing the work and removing avoidable barriers rather than excluding a group.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Eha Print has a capable applicant who uses a wheelchair, while the record desk is inaccessible. An accessible desk and route can remove the stated barrier to administrative work. The applicant’s relevant skill should be assessed instead of treating the inaccessible design as proof of inability.
